competitive_landscape: The coast is served today by a large diesel day-boat and liveaboard dive fleet plus resort transfer launches, with marina concessions held by Orascom (Abu Tig) and the Hurghada Marina operator. Demand is enormous and proven, but the day-boat experience is slow, crowded and in tension with the marine park's reef-mooring regime. There is no foiling incumbent.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The core resort-coast + marine-park network — Hurghada↔El Gouna (~13 nm), ↔Giftun (~9 nm), ↔Sahl Hasheesh (~12 nm) — sits comfortably inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope with marina charging; the zero-wake silent profile is the marine-park unlock.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR's 700 nm hybrid range covers the dive-coast and cross-gulf corridors — Soma Bay/Safaga (~25 nm), Sharm El Sheikh (~55 nm) and Marsa Alam (~120 nm) — with no charging-infrastructure dependency.

precedents.why_it_matters: Demonstrates electric foiling as the backbone of inter-island mobility at national scale — the proof that a foiling fleet can be the transport layer, not a novelty.

regulatory_note: The Egyptian Maritime Safety Authority / Ministry of Transport govern vessel class + cabotage; the Red Sea Governorate handles tourism; the Red Sea Protectorates (EEAA) govern the Giftun marine park (anchoring, wake, mooring-buoy regime — a clear zero-wake differentiator). Cross-border corridors to non-Egyptian ports are out of scope.
seasonality: Operable year-round — a key Red Sea advantage; the binding variables are strong summer northerly winds creating afternoon chop and rare winter storms. Morning calm favours early-departure island runs. No cyclone/typhoon exposure.

summary: Egypt's Red Sea Riviera is one of the Mediterranean-world's great mass-tourism coasts. Hurghada anchors a string of resort towns drawing tens of millions of visitors a year, and El Gouna — Orascom's master-planned town-on-lagoons just north — is among the most sophisticated marina-resort developments in the region, anchored by Abu Tig Marina. South run Sahl Hasheesh, Soma Bay and the dive port of Safaga; offshore lie the Giftun Islands marine park (Mahmya, Orange Bay), the day-trip island-hopping core reached today by slow diesel day-boats. The longer corridors — cross-gulf to Sharm El Sheikh and south to Marsa Alam — are Quanta-LR territory. A foiling-electric layer flies above the Red Sea chop, silent and zero-wake over the fragile reefs, collapsing the island-hopping pain in a weather-reliable, year-round basin.
tagline: A mature mass-tourism + dive coast with a master-planned marina town (El Gouna) and a fragile-reef marine park offshore — island-hopping on slow diesel day-boats, year-round sun.
